companies.label: Meituan
companies.metric_name: Core Local Commerce segment operating profit/(loss)
companies.metric_basis: Meituan's disclosed '核心本地商业' (Core Local Commerce) segment operating profit/loss, which bundles food delivery, Meituan Instashopping (instant retail) and in-store/hotel/travel — the segment absorbing nearly all delivery-war subsidy costs
companies.latest_signal: After regulators halted large-scale 'involution' subsidies in mid-2026, Core Local Commerce swung back to a RMB5.7bn operating profit in Q2 2026 (+52.3% YoY vs Q2 2025's RMB3.7bn), with margin recovering from -3.2% in Q1 to +7.9%; Meituan still holds >60% delivery GTV share, suggesting it did not blink first.

companies.label: Alibaba
companies.metric_name: Taobao Shangou (Flash Sale)/Ele.me instant-retail EBITA loss
companies.metric_basis: Alibaba does not disclose a standalone instant-commerce P&L; figure is the Taobao Shangou/Ele.me EBITA loss estimated by sell-side (CICC/Goldman) and corroborated in management commentary on the decline of China Commerce Group's adjusted EBITA, which blends core Taobao/Tmall CMR with instant-retail investment

periods.src: CICC estimate, cited in financial press around Alibaba's Nov 2025 call (FY26 Q2)
CICC estimate, cited around Alibaba FY26 Q3 period
Analyst estimate discussed on Alibaba FY26 Q4 call, 2026-05-14

companies.latest_signal: On the Aug 2026 call management said Taobao Shangou unit economics improved 'significantly' and loss narrowed ~RMB8bn q/q to ~RMB10bn; by October per-order losses were reported down ~50% versus July-August, with a stated target of UE breakeven by FY2027 and EBITA breakeven around FY2029. FY27 Q2 (Jul-Sep 2026) results, which would show the Double 11 subsidy push, had not yet been released as of 2026-11-11.

companies.label: JD.com
companies.metric_basis: JD's disclosed '新业务' (New Businesses) segment operating loss, covering JD Takeaway (food delivery), JD Daojia, Jingxi and overseas operations
companies.latest_signal: Loss has narrowed for four straight quarters as JD pulled back delivery marketing spend (~-22% q/q by Q3'25) and shifted JD Takeaway toward a 'lighter-asset' model; CFO Sandy Xu called it a 'clear profitability inflection point,' but the pace of q/q improvement slowed sharply (RMB4.3bn narrowing in Q1 2026 vs only RMB0.5bn in Q2 2026), and Q3 2026 results (due ~mid-Nov) will show the Double 11 spend test.

war_summary: Subsidy intensity peaked in mid-to-late 2025 through early 2026 and has clearly receded since, driven by Beijing's 'anti-involution' (反内卷) regulatory pressure on disorderly low-price competition in catering and instant retail. Meituan blinked least — its Core Local Commerce segment already flipped back to profit in Q2 2026 while defending >60% delivery GTV share — whereas JD and Alibaba are the ones visibly throttling investment: JD's New Businesses loss has narrowed every quarter since Q3 2025 (deceleration in Q2 2026 notwithstanding), and Alibaba's Taobao Shangou/Ele.me loss has roughly tracked the same path (from ~RMB37bn to ~RMB10bn/quarter) while management pushes out full EBITA breakeven to around FY2029. Double 11 2026 and the pending Q3 2026 reports (JD/Meituan due mid-to-late November) are the next test of whether narrowing holds or subsidies reflare.
